requirements.acceptance: Conversing characters orient their gaze towards one another.
Gaze changes when the other character moves; it is not a fixed head pose.
Visible blink/return cycles are staggered between actors.
Small pupil movements occur between major gaze changes.
Occasional brief glances return towards the conversation partner.
Eye response leads the slower head response on a new target.
Bounded head/torso movement supports the current speaker without turning the player root.
Listeners show facial, nod and gesture responses.
Long exchanges contain varied listening and idle motion.
No detached second opening appears below the original lip line during dialogue.
Only the aligned mouth/rim and appropriate teeth are visible; neutral interior is hidden.
All intended jaw/lip/interior morph bindings receive consistent speech values.
Opening/rounding follows the actual paused dialogue audio clock.
Mouth shapes interpolate smoothly without abrupt pops.
Speech weights settle below 0.015 and interior/teeth hide after the line.
Surprise, anger, fear, confidence, sadness, determination and happiness are visibly supported.
Expressions match the current speaker/listener and narrative context.
Changing an expression does not replace the spoken opening/rounding channel.
Standing characters show restrained breathing/postural movement.
Walk phase responds to actual travel and stops when blocked.
Foreground and crowd run poses follow actual travelled distance.
Heading follows the short angular path with bounded turn rate and blended stops.
Subtle body language supports retained hand gestures and prop ownership.
Long lines retain forward gesture movement and do not freeze at a held tail.
Listening includes occasional nods/reactions and posture variation.
Characters remain grounded and stable at rest and during route movements.
Calibrated walk/run timing matches movement; visible sliding is investigated.
Idle/listen/speak/walk/run/action changes blend without locked or duplicated actions.
Wide shots establish each important location.
Medium framing supports speaking gestures without clipping.
Conversation close-ups show eyes and mouth clearly.
Two-shots show the conversation relationship and spacing.
Shoulder coverage frames both participants without hiding the speaking face.
The listener is shown at appropriate dialogue beats.
Goliath has appropriate low-angle/scale-establishing coverage.
Moves/FOV transitions are stable and controlled; authored cuts are intentional.
Shots correspond to actual dialogue or combat state.
Cinematic cameras return control and do not obstruct movement or combat.
Warm key, reflected fill and grounded shadows improve character separation.
Skin, cloth, hair, leather and terrain retain appropriate roughness/detail.
Original surface grain and restrained vegetation movement improve existing environments.
Sky/fog/breeze add depth without obscuring gameplay.
Characters and near/far environment remain distinguishable.
Opening, audience, challenge, earned hit/fall and conclusion receive clear coverage.
Dialogue and mouth states share one source clock across pause/resume.
Retained music, weapon, movement and environmental effects suit the active scene.
Restart/rapid input cannot leave overlapping old speech schedules.
Required assets load reliably; facial shaders warm before the first spoken line.
Measured unrecorded laptop scene maintains the agreed 30 FPS target; stalls are reported.
Shared face ownership/detail textures, audio de-duplication and cleanup avoid unnecessary retained work.
Performance changes preserve faces, art direction, controls and rendering correctness.
